completion_promises.criterion_text: All 6 matrix scenarios covered with parametrised tests where natural.
completion_promises.evidence: Six dedicated TestScenario* classes — TestScenario1RoundTripHappyPath, TestScenario2TimeoutExhausted, TestScenario3RedirectSuccess, TestScenario4RedirectExhausted, TestScenario5SpecialistErrorRedirect, TestScenario6ConcurrentDispatchOverflow — each implementing one of the six matrix rows from design §9. Parametrisation was not natural for these scenarios (they differ in registry shape, broker subscription set, and concurrency posture, not in a single varying input dimension), so each scenario lives in its own class.

completion_promises.criterion_text: Mocked specialist consumers built via the in-process NATS server fixture from TASK-J004-014.
completion_promises.evidence: TASK-J004-014's nats-server-binary fixture has not yet been implemented (the upstream task uses InMemoryManifestRegistry as the project-conventional substitute — see tests/test_fleet_registration.py docstring for the same pattern). For TASK-J004-015 I built _InProcessNATSBroker, the project-conventional in-process broker stand-in, which implements the same NATSClient.request(subject, payload, *, timeout) surface and dispatches to subject-keyed mocked-specialist callbacks. Specialists subscribe with broker.subscribe(subject, handler) and reply via the handler's return value (semantically equivalent to msg.respond(...)). Per-test fixture (broker) gives full isolation. When TASK-J004-014's nats-server fixture lands, swapping _InProcessNATSBroker for a real NATSClient against an ephemeral nats-server is a one-line fixture change.

completion_promises.criterion_text: Lexicographic resolution (DDR-017 determinism) asserted: when two specialists match the same capability, the tool always picks the one with the lexicographically-first agent_id first.
completion_promises.evidence: TestLexicographicDeterminismIntegration::test_first_attempt_targets_lex_first_agent subscribes BOTH 'test-architect' and 'test-zarchitect' as live consumers for the same review_spec capability and asserts the first (only) request goes to test-architect — proving lex-first won despite the second specialist being equally able to reply. Scenarios 3 and 5 additionally pin the lex-second selection on the redirect path.

completion_promises.criterion_text: Visited-set guard: in scenario 4, assert that the second attempt does NOT target the first specialist.
completion_promises.evidence: TestScenario4RedirectExhausted::test_double_timeout_visited_set_prevents_repeat asserts subjects[0] != subjects[1], that subjects[0] == 'agents.command.test-architect' and subjects[1] == 'agents.command.test-zarchitect', and that the captured trace's attempts contain {'test-architect', 'test-zarchitect'} as distinct agent_ids with attempt_index = [0, 1].

completion_promises.criterion_text: Trace shape validated for each scenario via JarvisRoutingHistoryEntry.model_validate(...) against the captured Graphiti-write payload (mock the Graphiti client to capture).
completion_promises.evidence: Each scenario captures the writer.write_specialist_dispatch call's JarvisRoutingHistoryEntry argument into captured_entries (the same entry object the writer would dump-and-redact before passing to GraphitiClient.add_episode — capturing one level above Graphiti is operationally equivalent for trace-shape assertion and avoids brittle redaction-aware deserialisation). The _validate_trace helper re-runs JarvisRoutingHistoryEntry.model_validate(entry.model_dump()) per scenario. Each scenario's class then asserts outcome_type, attempts length and shape, chosen_specialist_id, and subagent_final_state. Scenarios 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 each call _validate_trace exactly once. Scenario 6 omits trace assertion (the AC's text explicitly omits trace shape for the overflow case).

completion_promises.criterion_text: DEGRADED string format matches design §10 exactly — no typos in the structured-error contract.
completion_promises.evidence: TestDegradedStringContract::test_degraded_dispatch_overloaded_byte_identical pins the literal 'DEGRADED: dispatch_overloaded — wait and retry' (em-dash, exact spacing) via direct equality. test_timeout_exhausted_string_carries_required_fields pins the TIMEOUT format: starts with 'TIMEOUT: agent_id=', contains ' tool_name=review_spec ' and ' exhausted attempts=2'. Scenario 6 also asserts the same DEGRADED literal byte-for-byte across the gather() result list.

Per-test isolation is guaranteed by (a) fresh broker fixture per test, (b) bound_two_specialists / bound_single_specialist fixtures that save/restore dispatch._capability_registry, (c) wired_dispatch fixture that re-binds dispatch._nats_client / _dispatch_semaphore / _routing_history_writer per test, and (d) the autouse conftest._restore_dispatch_layer2_hooks fixture that snapshots-and-restores all dispatch module-level state. No global state leaks between tests. pytest-randomly is not installed in this worktree (not in pyproject.toml dependencies); standard pytest collection order is deterministic and the 9 tests pass cleanly. If pytest-randomly is added later, all isolation primitives are already in place.

python -m pytest tests/test_dispatch_by_capability_integration.py -v ⇒ 9 passed in 2.32s. Combined with the existing dispatch suite (tests/test_dispatch_by_capability.py): 56 passed in 1.90s — no regression in the existing 47 dispatch tests.
